statement: A company having a share capital may be incorporated as a private company if its constitution restricts the right to transfer its shares and limits the number of its members to not more than 50, counting joint holders of shares as one person and not counting current employees, or continuing former employees, of the company or its subsidiary.
caveat: The member cap and transfer restriction live in the constitution, and section 18(4) lets a private company alter them by special resolution only within the private-company limits. Exceeding them puts the company outside private status; see section 31 on conversion.
